thesis: Mohnish Pabrai argues that the 1626 sale of Manhattan for $24 was a great deal for the Native Americans because the failure to compound that money at a modest 7% annual return resulted in a massive loss of value over time. He illustrates that understanding compounding, such as using the Rule of 72, is essential for investors and entrepreneurs to align their capital allocation strategies effectively.
